foodDescription: Large zeppelin-shaped dumplings of grated potato filled with meat or curd cheese, served with sour cream and bacon. The national dish, and very filling.
A bright pink cold soup of beets, kefir, cucumber, and dill, served with hot boiled potatoes. Summer’s most famous dish, and a source of national pride.
Half-moon pastries filled with mutton or other fillings, brought by the Karaim, a small Turkic people settled at nearby Trakai in the 1300s.
A baked pudding of grated potato, eggs, and bacon, cut into squares and served with sour cream.
Strips of dark rye bread fried and rubbed with garlic, often with a cheese dip. The classic beer snack.
Pancakes of grated potato fried crisp and served with sour cream, or filled with meat.
Pig intestines stuffed with grated potato and baked. Old-fashioned country food.
A hard, aged Lithuanian cheese, sold at a few to dozens of months old. There is a Džiugas shop in the old town.
A tall, spiky cake built up by dripping batter onto a turning spit over a fire. Made for weddings and celebrations.
Dense, slightly sweet rye bread, often with caraway seeds. Served with almost every meal.
A fizzy, lightly sweet drink fermented from rye bread, like Russian kvass. Sold cold in summer.
Honey wine, one of the oldest drinks in Lithuania, made in both mild and strong versions.
